For $R=16$, this is 4096 operations per voxel.

*   **Memory Complexity:** Proportional to the size of the core tensor ($R_1 R_2 R_3$) plus the factor matrices ($I_1 R_1 + I_2 R_2 + I_3 R_3$).
*   **Strengths:** Captures non-axis aligned features at different scales better than wavelet transforms using the same amount of coefficients.

*   **When to use:** Interactive large volume visualization, microstructural analysis where specific features at different scales need to be highlighted, and scenarios requiring high compression ratios with feature preservation.
Tensor Approximation was introduced to Direct Volume Rendering (DVR) by Suter et al. [SIM* 11], building on earlier work in tensor decomposition [KB09].
It applies SVD/PCA-like tools to volume data by interpreting blocks as tensors.
The method was further developed to include tensor-specific quantization and optimized GPU reconstruction [SMP13].
